stories.title: BRICS Parliamentary Forum Condemns Pahalgam Terror Attack; Calls for Zero Tolerance and End To Cross-Border Terror
stories.summary: The forum expressed deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in the Middle East/West Asia and called for exercising maximum restraint.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

opening: The forum expressed deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in the Middle East/West Asia and called for exercising maximum restraint.

New Delhi, Oct 27: The two-day conclave of the BRICS Parliamentary Forum on Tuesday adopted a joint declaration strongly condemning the 2025 Pahalgam attack and all acts of terrorism as it pledged to combat the menace in all its forms and manifestations and also stressed on non-intervention in the internal affairs of any country.
body: The joint declaration, announced by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, also condemned the imposition of unilateral economic and secondary sanctions saying such coercive measures have far reaching negative implications on human rights, including the right to development, health and food security of people.

The BRICS Parliamentary Forum supported a comprehensive reform of the United Nations, including its Security Council, saying this reform should make it more just, equitable, democratic, representative, effective, and efficient, better reflecting contemporary realities and the needs of the international community.
"We express strong condemnation of any acts of terrorism as criminal and unjustifiable, regardless of their motivation, whenever, wherever and by whomsoever committed.
We condemn in the strongest terms the terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir (in Pahalgam) on 22 April 2025, during which 26 people were killed and many more injured.
"We reaffirm our commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, including the cross-border movement of terrorists, terrorism financing and safe havens," the declaration read.

The Forum said terrorism should not be associated with any religion, nationality, civilisation or ethnic group and that all those involved in terrorist activities and their support must be held accountable and brought to justice in accordance with relevant national and international law.
"We urge to ensure zero tolerance for terrorism and reject double standards in countering terrorism.

We emphasise the primary responsibility of States in combating terrorism and that global efforts to prevent and counter terrorist threats must fully comply with their obligations under international law, including the Charter of the UN...," it read.

The Forum said it looks forward to further deepening counter-terrorism cooperation and calls for an expeditious finalisation and adoption of the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism in the UN framework and concerted actions against all UN-designated terrorists and terrorist entities.

"We reaffirm our adherence to the principles of sovereign equality, mutual respect, non-intervention in internal affairs, and the peaceful settlement of international disputes, as enshrined in the United Nations Charter, as essential foundations for global stability, peace and development," it said.

The Forum reaffirmed its unwavering support for the peaceful resolution of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict based on the two-state solution, with the two States living side by side, in peace and security, in accordance with international law and relevant United Nations resolutions.
It asserted the right of the Palestinian people to self-determination, freedom, and an independent, sovereign State.

The Forum expressed deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in West Asia and, recalling the respective national positions, called for exercising maximum restraint, as well as avoiding actions that could further aggravate the situation.

It strongly condemned all violations of international humanitarian law, including deliberate attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure, including in BRICS member states, as well as the denial or obstruction of humanitarian access and the targeting of humanitarian personnel.
Iran and United Arab Emirates, which are directly involved with the West Asia conflict, are members of the BRICS.
Apart from India, other member nations of the BRICS are: Brazil, Russia, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia and South Africa.
The Forum underlined the need to address accountability for all violations of international humanitarian law.
"We recognise international efforts undertaken by BRICS members to promote respect for, adherence to, and effective implementation of international humanitarian law," it said.

Recognising the urgency of addressing climate change, the BRICS parliamentary body calls for intensifying efforts, through dialogue and international cooperation, to implement nationally determined contributions, strengthen mitigation and adaptation efforts, with a view to achieving the objectives of the UNFCCC and the goals of its Paris Agreement as applicable.
The Forum acknowledge the transformative potential of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI) and information and communication technologies (ICTs).

"We emphasise the necessity of ensuring the open, safe, secure, stable, equitably accessible, peaceful and interoperable use and development of ICTs environment while respecting sovereignty and national security of each country.

"In addition, promoting energy efficiency of AI systems, fostering AI science and innovation, leveraging AI for economic growth and social good and mitigating potential risks would be essential for promoting a just, fair, equitable and prosperous future of all countries, especially those of Global South," it said.

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab: 50 trains cancelled, thousands evacuated as Andhra, Odisha brace for impact
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab: 50 trains cancelled, thousands evacuated as Andhra, Odisha brace for impact
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Strong winds have begun sweeping through Visakhapatnam and Kakinada, while Srikakulam and other northern coastal districts are expected to receive heavy rainfall accompanied by powerful winds.

Bhubaneswar/Amaravati: Andhra Pradesh and Odisha have stepped up emergency preparations as very severe cyclonic storm Arnab approaches the eastern coast, with nearly 4,000 relief shelters readied, thousands of residents being evacuated and disaster response teams placed on high alert ahead of its expected landfall on Wednesday.
The approaching cyclone has already disrupted rail and air services, prompting the cancellation of at least 50 trains and two IndiGo flights.
Restrictions have also been imposed on several coastal roads as authorities race to minimise damage and prevent casualties.
According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the cyclone was located approximately 140 km southeast of Kakinada and 170 km south of Visakhapatnam at 2.30 pm on Tuesday.
Moving at a speed of 18 kmph, the storm is expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, near Yanam, by Wednesday forenoon.
Heavy rainfall and strong winds have already begun affecting parts of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, while the cyclone's influence is also being felt in West Bengal and neighbouring Jharkhand.
The Andhra Pradesh government has established 2,131 cyclone shelters across 20 districts as part of extensive preparations to deal with the approaching storm.
Authorities have placed 1,087 medical teams on standby and arranged 8,281 emergency hospital beds and 1,274 ambulances in areas expected to experience severe weather.
In a precautionary measure, 1,351 pregnant women have been shifted to hospitals to ensure access to medical assistance during the cyclone.
The administration has also stocked two months' worth of essential commodities at 14,686 ration shops to prevent shortages if transport and supply networks are disrupted.
Cyclone warnings are being sent continuously to the mobile phones of approximately 2.70 crore people across the state.

article_sentences: Bapatla district Collector Dr. V. Vinod Kumar has issued emergency helpline numbers to help people seek assistance during cyclonic conditions, heavy rain and other emergency situations.
According to a statement issued on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), the district administration has established a 24-hour control room to respond to emergencies.
The public can contact the District Control Room at 08643-220226.
People can also reach the WhatsApp helpline at 8712417880 and share their geographical location to facilitate assistance.
For power supply-related emergencies, the Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Corporation Limited (APCPDCL) has provided separate contact numbers for different areas.
The Bapatla Circle helpline is 92814 13774, while the numbers for the Bapatla and Repalle divisions are 94910 52945 and 94408 17597.
The administration has also announced helpline numbers for Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO) offices.
The Repalle RDO office can be contacted at 08648-293795 or 94407 80426.
The Chirala RDO office number is 87126 55910, while the Bapatla RDO office can be reached at 94938 03524.
The district administration has urged people to use these helplines to report emergencies and seek assistance during adverse weather conditions.

stories.title: Stand Together, Stay Safe: AP Govt Appeals to People Ahead of Cyclone Arnab

article_sentences: The exact information on whether or not it will be an extremely severe cyclone would be available in about two hours, IMD officials said.
Cyclone Arnab, as of now, is unlikely to intensify further into an extremely severe cyclone.
The very severe cyclonic storm moved west-northwestwards at a speed of 20 kmph during the preceding six hours and was centred over the west-central Bay of Bengal at 8.30 am on Tuesday.
Though the indications are that it may not be an extremely severe cyclone, the administration has been put on high alert and efforts to meet the challenges are being made to meet any eventuality.
The Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu directed the officials to ensure evacuations and take all precautionary measures to avoid loss of life and property.
Already, over 1300 pregnant women have been shifted to hospitals.
In Kakinada district's Pithapuram area, rising sea waves have reached coastal areas, hitting Uppada, Konapapet and Moolapet, causing concern among residents.
According to the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA), the cyclone's effects had begun to be felt, with heavy rainfall likely shortly in north coastal Andhra districts.
Srikakulam district was likely to witness heavy rainfall accompanied by strong winds, while strong winds had begun in coastal districts such as Visakhapatnam and Kakinada.

CM, who is monitoring the cyclone continuously, directed officials to shift people living in low-lying areas to safer locations, ensure essential supplies at relief camps and minimise cyclone-related damage, as Cyclone Arnab is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam on October 28, with heavy rainfall expected in north coastal districts.

"The cyclone, which was earlier classified as a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal, has intensified into a very severe cyclonic storm and is expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts near Yanam, between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, by the forenoon of October 28," the Met department said in an official press release.

The system was located 220 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam, 240 km east-southeast of Kakinada, 340 km east-southeast of Machilipatnam, 370 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha and 410 km east of Bapatla, the IMD said.

stories.headline: We know everything, will examine: Supreme Court on plea against Election Commission
stories.title: We know everything, will examine: Supreme Court on plea against Election Commission
stories.summary: We know everything, will examine: Supreme Court on plea against Election Commission
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Supreme Court directed the ECI and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to respond to the Opposition's plea as it posted the next hearing on November 17.

The Supreme Court on Tuesday said it was aware of all developments and would examine all aspects of the allegations against the Election Commission, as it heard a batch of petitions questioning the poll body's functioning and alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

"We know everything, we will examine," Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said when senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, appearing for Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders, urged the court to direct the preservation of file notings and internal communications to establish whether key decisions were taken unanimously or unilaterally.

The bench, comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, adjourned the hearing and granted the petitioners 10 days to file their rejoinder to the counter-affidavit submitted by the Election Commission on Monday.
The matter was tentatively listed for further hearing on November 17.

The petitions challenge the functioning of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and question whether the Commission's decisions, including those related to the SIR exercise, were taken in accordance with the constitutional and statutory framework governing the poll body.

During the hearing, Singhvi argued that the dispute centred on the decision-making process within the Election Commission, particularly whether the decisions concerning the electoral roll revision exercise had been taken after consultation among the commissioners.
"This whole issue depends on the decision-making process, consultation, and whether the decision was unanimous or not unanimous.
Let file notings, etc be preserved," Singhvi told the bench.
Responding to the submission, CJI Surya Kant said the court was aware of the developments and would examine the issues raised before it.

The preservation of internal records is significant to the petitioners' case, as they have alleged that several crucial decisions concerning the SIR exercise were taken in the name of the Commission despite objections from the other two Election Commissioners.

The allegations have emerged against the backdrop of a report by The Indian Express, which claimed that at least 14 important decisions related to the SIR exercise were taken despite objections recorded by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.

article_sentences: The State government is considering setting up an ‘Academic Election Commission’ on campuses to introduce constructive reforms in student union elections, Higher Education Minister Roji M. John said in the Keralam Assembly on Tuesday.

Replying to a submission by Uma Thomas, the Minister said the government supported campus politics but was committed to curbing unhealthy practices while not infringing on students’ democratic right to protest.

Student politics had been active in Keralam’s colleges since the freedom struggle and it had evolved through the formation of various student organisations and campaigns to protect democratic rights, he pointed out.
Healthy political interactions helped students develop leadership skills, assimilate democratic and constitutional values, all the while contributing to a vibrant and active campus environment.
However, in at least some institutions, the government has taken note that campus politics was taking an unhealthy turn, he said.
The government’s policy has been to curb such practices without curtailing students’ right to democratic protest, the Minister said.

Apart from revising the college election processes, the government was also introducing the ‘Sidharthan Student Distress App’, announced in the Budget and included in the 100-day action programme and the ‘Sidharthan Anti-Ragging and Student Welfare Act’, aimed at safeguarding student welfare, as part of its intensive efforts to check unhealthy practices on campuses.
The government’s policy was to encourage campus politics, but any activities that disrupt the peace and harmony on campuses will not be allowed, Mr. John said.

stories.title: Supreme Court Questions Centre Over Medicine Overpricing, Calls NPPA ‘Totally Defunct’
stories.summary: The Supreme Court today raised the Centre's eyebrows on the issue of over pricing of medicines and expressed its displeasure at the NPPA for its failure to bridge the gap between the drug MRP and the purchase price by the retailers.

article_sentences: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Tuesday questioned the Centre over the wide gap between the maximum retail price (MRP) of medicines and the price at which retailers purchase them, asking whether the government could justify what it described as “loot” and whether pharmaceutical manufacturers should be allowed to “run amok”.

A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta criticised the functioning of the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), describing it as seemingly “totally defunct”, and questioned why the drug pricing system appeared to favour manufacturers over patients.
The court reserved its verdict on two petitions concerning drug pricing, including pleas for stricter controls to ensure medicines remain affordable.
During the hearing, the Centre referred to its decision to cap the trade margin on anti-cancer drugs at 30 per cent of their maximum retail price.
The Bench, however, questioned why a uniform trade margin of 16 per cent could not be introduced for all medicines.
“The government policy is that entire ecosystem is not to be controlled,” Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, told the Bench.
The judges pointed to a medicine with a price to retailer (PTR) of Rs 15 but an MRP of Rs 250, questioning the justification for such a substantial difference.
“Can you show any justification for this loot,” the Bench asked, adding that the government was allowing the practice to continue under its watch.
When Bhati referred to the need for regulatory control, the court asked, “Should it be allowed to run amok?”
The law officer argued that medicine prices in India were among the lowest in the world.
However, the Bench questioned why the pricing system appeared to work in favour of pharmaceutical manufacturers.
“Why is the entire system working to help these people (manufacturers),” the judges asked.

stories.headline: Omar expands cabinet with 4 new ministers, triggers internal discontent and BJP criticism
stories.title: Omar expands cabinet with 4 new ministers, triggers internal discontent and BJP criticism
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 27: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah expanded his council of ministers on Tuesday with the induction of four new faces from the Kashmir valley, triggering internal party discontent and protests, even as the opposition BJP hit out at the ruling alliance over "regional and cultural imbalance". The four National Conference (NC) leaders, veteran politician Ali Mohammad Sagar, Mir Saifullah, Shameema Firdous, and Altaf Ahmad Wani (Kalloo), were administered the oath of office by Lt Governor Manoj Sinha at Lok Bhawan here. With all four inductees hailing from Kashmir, the expansion has shifted the balance of the cabinet in the two-year-old government heavily towards the valley. Seven ministers in the now 9-member council hail from Kashmir, while Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Chaudhary and Javaid Rana remain the only two representatives from the Jammu region. Independent MLA from Chhamb, Satish Sharma, was dropped from the cabinet to accommodate the new inductees. Ahead of the expansion, all ministers had formally submitted their resignations to the Chief Minister to facilitate the reshuffle. The maximum allowed strength of the JK council of ministers is nine, adhering to the statutory 10 per cent limit of the 90-member Assembly in the union territory. National Conference chief Farooq Abdullah said "a very good cabinet change has taken place. They (ministers) will work and try to ease the difficulties and problems of the people". The reshuffle sparked immediate anger among supporters of six-time NC MLA from Eidgah, Mubarak Gul, who staged a noisy protest outside the party headquarters at Nawa-e-Subah after his name was omitted from the cabinet list. Agitated workers raised slogans against the decision, calling it a grave injustice to a leader with 40 years of service. Before the swearing-in ceremony, Gul expressed his dismay to reporters, saying, "I will speak at an appropriate time. I have attended 20 oath ceremonies and every time I have been dropped. You can say I have been dropped again." In a swift bid to contain the mounting resentment, NC President Farooq Abdullah rushed to the party headquarters shortly after the ceremony and appointed Gul as the party's new general secretary, replacing Sagar, who joined the cabinet. "Party President Dr Farooq Abdullah sb today nominated senior party leader, MLA Idgah Mubarak Gul Sb as party's new General Secretary. Wishing Gul sb all the very best," NC spokesperson Imran Nabi Dar posted on X. Discontent was also voiced by another senior NC leader, Abdul Majid Bhat Larmi, who admitted feeling hurt at being left out but pledged loyalty to the party. "After all, we are human beings. The heart naturally feels hurt — there is no doubt about that. Here I am talking to you, but from inside, my heart is burning," an emotional Larmi said, adding that he accepted the leadership's decision. The expansion also drew sharp criticism from the BJP as the Leader of Opposition Sunil Sharma accused the Omar Abdullah-led government of creating a regional divide. "This is the first time that there is a regional and cultural imbalance," Sharma told reporters. "Governments have to take every community, region, and area along. Today, that was nowhere to be seen." Meanwhile, the Congress, an ally of the ruling coalition, opted to remain outside the government. JKPCC president Tariq Hamid Karra reaffirmed his party's stance, stating that the Congress will not join the council of ministers until statehood is fully restored to Jammu and Kashmir. Among the new inductees, Sagar — a seven-time MLA who took his oath in Urdu — has never lost an Assembly election since his debut in 1983. Saifullah, who won from Trehgam post-delimitation in 2024, alongside first-time ministers Wani (Pahalgam) and Firdous (Habbakadal), took their oath in English. Firdous, who also heads the NC's women’s wing, becomes the second woman minister in the cabinet alongside Sakina Itoo. The oath-taking ceremony was attended by Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, Speaker Abdul Rahim Rather, senior alliance leaders, and opposition MLAs from both the BJP and PDP. Satish Sharma remained absent from the swearing-in ceremony.

stories.headline: Why Most Medicines Kept Out Of Price Control Regime? Supreme Court Questions Centre, Reserves Order
stories.title: Why Most Medicines Kept Out Of Price Control Regime? Supreme Court Questions Centre, Reserves Order
stories.summary: “What stops you from taking control of the entire range of medicines and drugs?” SC asked the Centre.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: “What stops you from taking control of the entire range of medicines and drugs?” SC asked the Centre.

The Supreme Court on Tuesday questioned why the Union government was reluctant to bring a wider range of medicines under price control, observing that its reliance on market forces and concerns about pharmaceutical-industry growth cannot justify leaving patients exposed to medicine prices that may be hundreds of times higher than procurement costs.
“You are dealing with the lives of people, Ms. Bhati.
Don't take it as a commerce.
Treat it as a life of the poorest person of this country.
You are talking only in the terms of commerce, economic policy, this, that.

Is this a matter in which economic policy will be supreme as compared to the life of the citizens at large?” Justice Sandeep Mehta asked Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, who was defending the Centre's pharmaceutical pricing policy.

The Court reserved its order in the case concerning regulation of medicine prices after questioning the Centre over the substantial difference between the maximum retail price (MRP) of medicines and the prices at which retailers procure them.
The Court also questioned why a large proportion of medicines remained outside the stricter price-control regime under the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013 (DPCO).

A bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta repeatedly asked Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati to explain why the government permitted manufacturers to print MRPs several times higher than the prices charged to dealers and retailers.

During the hearing, Justice Sandeep Mehta recounted an incident in which a medical dealer, whose wife was undergoing cancer treatment at a prominent hospital, wanted to procure a chemotherapy injection for her at the dealer price of ₹11,000.
The hospital refused to administer the injection and charged ₹1.3 lakh for it, he said.

article_sentences: Guwahati: The Chief Minister of Assam, Himanta Biswa Sarma has announced that the Assam Cabinet has approved a 12% horizontal reservation for eligible former Agniveers in specified posts across key state departments.

Sharing the update on social media, Sarma said the initiative aims to recognise the service and discipline of those who have served the nation and provide them with further employment opportunities in Assam.
The reservation will benefit ex-Agniveers who are domiciles of Assam and have completed their full four-year tenure under the Agnipath scheme.
As per the announcement, the reservation will apply to specified posts in the Assam.
Police, the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), the Forest Department, prisons, Home Guards, Fire and Emergency Services, and the Excise Department, among other designated services.
The state government has also indicated that annual recruitment drives for eligible candidates will begin in 2027.

Emphasising the importance of the decision, Sarma said the move was aimed at valuing the discipline and dedication of former Agniveers while creating new avenues for them to continue serving the state.

The initiative is expected to provide eligible former Agniveers with additional opportunities to join state government services after completing their military tenure, subject to the applicable recruitment rules and eligibility criteria.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) sought a response from Rahul Gandhi and others on a plea which alleged the Congress leader pushed a pregnant journalist during a march to the apex court on October 12.
The plea was mentioned before a Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi, which issued notice to Mr. Gandhi and others.
Senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia, who mentioned the matter, said an application has been filed in a pending petition.
A female journalist was manhandled in the court premises, Mr. Bhatia submitted.
"Respondent No. 4 [Rahul Gandhi] suddenly pushed her towards the gate, with such force that she lost her balance and fell, and had to break the fall with her hands.

The push was delivered openly, in a crowded place, in the presence of security personnel, journalists and other persons, despite her express pleas, and was not a mere jostle of the crowd,” the plea submitted.
The application filed in a pending plea sought directions seeking immediate registration of an FIR against Mr. Gandhi and all others involved in the “assault” besides seeking compensation.
Mr. Bhatia, on October 16, also urged the Bench to consider the matter.
"A lady journalist was pushed by Rahul Gandhi in the Supreme Court precincts.
She was three months pregnant and had to be hospitalised," Mr. Bhatia had argued, adding that the Supreme Court may take cognisance of the matter.

On October 12, Mr. Gandhi and several prominent Opposition leaders, accompanied by their supporters, reached the Supreme Court to file a plea over alleged large-scale voter deletions and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
The national capital has witnessed several protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the SIR process.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Issues Notice To Centre On Pleas Challenging Mandate To Sing Six-Stanza Version Of Vande Mataram
stories.title: Supreme Court Issues Notice To Centre On Pleas Challenging Mandate To Sing Six-Stanza Version Of Vande Mataram
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today issued notice on two petitions challenging the Union Government's January 28 and July 9, 2026 orders prescribing a six-stanza version of 'Vande Mataram' for singing and playing on specified occasions.

One petition has been filed by BD Borkar, a Scheduled Caste Buddhist, Ambedkarite activist and former National President of the All India Backward and Minority Communities Employees Federation (BAMCEF).
The other petition is filed by a former IAS officer from Kerala, Balakrishnan Sathyabhama Mavoji, who belongs to the Scheduled Caste community.
As soon as the matters were taken, the bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana issued notice to the Centre.
Dr G Mohan Gopal appeared for the petitioners.

"By imposing sectarian prayer to particular Goddesses of one particular religion as the National Song of India, the Impugned Orders convert the character of the polity of India from a 'secular republic' to a 'theocracy'," Borkar stated in the petition.

According to him, such an imposition will "irreversibly deepen communal division and conflict in India by outraging the religious and spiritual feelings of minority religions including the religion of the petitioner (Buddhism);" The move, it is contended, makes a "a mockery of the foundational Constitutional basic structure features of fraternity and secularism."

The petitioners contend that the Centre has effectively replaced the two-stanza version of 'Vande Mataram', which has traditionally been sung at national functions since Independence, with the six-stanza composition appearing in Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's novel Anandamath.
The petitioners argue that the two-stanza version, which predates the novel Anandamath, is distinct from the six-stanza composition incorporated into the novel in 1881.
According to the petition, the original two stanzas describe the natural beauty of the motherland, whereas the additional four stanzas invoke Hindu goddesses Durga, Lakshmi and Saraswati.
According to them, Anandamath is a novel "filled with violent and hateful invective against Muslims", and the six-stanza version of the song is used in the context of a war cry.
Leaders like Mahatma Gandhi and Rabindranath Tagore had objected to the adoption of all six stanzas, and the first two stanzas were accepted as a formula put forth by Tagore.

stories.headline: Supreme Court seeks Centre's response on news publishers' plea challenging data protection law
stories.title: Supreme Court seeks Centre's response on news publishers' plea challenging data protection law
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The plea seeks to strike down several provisions of the data protection law as unconstitutional.

New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Tuesday issued a notice to the Centre on a petition challenging various provisions of the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act and its accompanying DPDP Rules, which allegedly infringe upon press freedom and the right to information.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued the notice after hearing arguments from senior advocate Madhavi Divan, who appeared for the Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA).
The court has listed the matter for further hearing on November 17, alongside other pending petitions.
It highlights that the absence of a specific exemption for journalistic activities could severely impede news reporting, weaken investigative journalism, and compromise source confidentiality.

During the proceedings, Divan described the petition as perhaps the first comprehensive challenge by what she termed the "legacy media", distinguishing traditional news organisations from citizen journalists.
"This is perhaps the first comprehensive petition by what we call legacy media.
There has been some debate over citizen journalists.
We are the traditional, conventional legacy media," she said.
The senior lawyer urged the bench to issue a notice on the application seeking an interim stay of the challenged provisions.

Divan argued that the law’s consent requirements could render routine news gathering and reporting unworkable, especially when journalists report on individuals who refuse to consent to the processing of their personal data.
"If I am left to the mercy of the data principal as to whether he or she will give consent, how will news be reported?" she asked.
